title: ANDS Studio — eCTD module builder
walkthrough:
You open a dossier and land on its Module 1 workspace, laid out in three columns.

The left column is the section tree. Its header shows an "M1" badge, the module name, a progress bar, and an "X/Y required placed" count. A collapsed "Status key" button, marked with a help icon, reveals a tooltip legend of what each status word means. Below, each section row carries a status icon with a hover tooltip, the section title and number, and a second line reading "Required" or "Optional," an optional lifecycle operator, and the status word. Rows where AI drafting is available show a small sparkle icon. Two collapsible buckets at the bottom hold sections "Not in this submission model" and "Marked N/A by you."

The center column shows the selected section. An eyebrow reads "Module 1 · Section 1.2.2 · required," and where the leaf is placed ("Placed at … · leaf …"). Below sit the title, a one-line purpose, and a "What Health Canada needs here" teach box with the guidance. A collapsed "Format & source" expander holds the format, bilingual flag, and a "Health Canada guidance ↗" link, and a collapsed "eCTD in plain language" primer explains leaf, sequence, working vs active, and new/replace/append/delete.

An action bar offers toggle buttons: "Upload," "Author in-app," and "Mark N/A." Upload shows a drop zone ("Drop a file or click to choose") with the accepted formats; bilingual sections show separate English and French zones. Choosing "Author in-app" opens a form. For AI-eligible sections a mode toggle appears first — "Draft with AI" or "Fill the form." A note explains the form produces a PDF/A leaf at the eCTD position, naming the lifecycle operation, that known facts are pre-filled, and that fields tagged "example — replace this" show greyed example text you must replace. You edit the fields and click "Author [title] →" ("Authoring…" while busy), or "Review vs Health Canada" first. A review panel then reads "Health Canada review: no blocking content gaps." on pass, or "N to fix, M to check." with a bulleted list, each item carrying a suggested edit and an "HC guidance ↗" link.

The saved document card lists the filename, size, and "fingerprint md5" fragment, a provenance chip, and a "Download" link. While a draft holds example values or is an AI draft, a red banner reads "Not yet filable — review required." A sample draft clears automatically once no example values remain; an AI draft needs the button "I have reviewed this AI draft — it is my content." Actions surface toast notifications ("… placed at leaf …," "… confirmed as your content").

The right column leads with a "Ready to transmit" card showing a "● READY" or "● BLOCKED" status. If any sample or AI drafts are unconfirmed, a red banner reads "N sample/AI draft value(s) not yet filable." Three flags follow — "Documents," "Fee," and "Structural check" — each an icon plus label, with the Structural-check tooltip stating it is not Health Canada's official eValidator and to run eValidator before transmitting. A line notes how many items are still needed to file. Below sits a Draft completeness check, then one-line expanders for the "Submission tower (3D module view)," "Submission lifecycle & deficiency clock," "eCTD sequences & package export" (which force-opens and shows "export blocked" when blocked), a Module 1 "Bilingual / XML Product Monograph detail," and "Collaboration & task assignments." Selecting another section in the tree swaps the center panel; completing work updates the progress bar and the row's status icon.
